questions.q: What is the main point of this capstone, according to the kickoff lesson?
options: To learn an entirely new set of advanced techniques not covered earlier
To run the same ideas this course already taught — features, splits, training, honest evaluation — start to finish on one real dataset
To memorize the scikit-learn API reference
To build the largest possible model for the dataset
questions.explain: The capstone deliberately introduces nothing new. It's the course's existing ideas — features and labels, train/test splitting, model fitting, honest evaluation — applied end to end by the student.

questions.q: Which dataset does this capstone use, and why was it chosen?
options: A scraped social media dataset with millions of rows
Breast Cancer Wisconsin (Diagnostic) — a real, built-in scikit-learn dataset with 569 samples and 30 features, needing no download or cleanup
A randomly generated synthetic dataset with no real-world meaning
A proprietary dataset the student must purchase
questions.explain: The dataset ships inside scikit-learn itself (load_breast_cancer), is small, has no missing values, and gives a genuine binary classification task — so lesson time goes to ML decisions, not data wrangling.

questions.q: Why does the kickoff lesson insist the `StandardScaler` be fit on the training split only, not the full dataset?
options: Because fitting it on all the data is slightly slower
Fitting it on the full dataset before splitting leaks information from the test set into training, the same data leakage failure named back in lesson 16
Because StandardScaler can only be fit once per Python session
There's no real reason, it's just a stylistic convention
questions.explain: Fitting any preprocessing step on the full dataset before splitting lets statistics from the test set influence training — exactly the data leakage pattern chapter 3's lesson 16 covered.

questions.q: Why is `LogisticRegression` chosen as the capstone's baseline model instead of something more complex?
options: It's the only classifier scikit-learn provides
It guarantees the highest possible accuracy on any dataset
It's a simple, interpretable starting point chosen on purpose — the same role classification was introduced in back in lesson 7
Complex models are against the rules for student capstones
questions.explain: The goal is a correctly built, correctly evaluated baseline, not the fanciest model available — LogisticRegression is picked deliberately as a simple, readable starting point.

questions.q: What does "no cherry-picking," one of the capstone's ground rules, actually require?
options: Reporting the full confusion matrix and precision/recall for both classes, not just whichever single metric looks best
Selecting only successful test cases to report
Running the model multiple times and keeping only the best run
Avoiding evaluation entirely
questions.explain: Lesson 29 is held to reporting accuracy, the full confusion matrix, and precision/recall for both classes — the complete picture, not a single flattering number.
